title: AMD Stock Is Crashing - Is It A Buy Now?
creator: Daniel Pronk
summary: Daniel Pronk answers the question in the title — AMD is down 36% from its all-time highs — by walking through AMD's latest quarter and comparing it with Nvidia on fundamentals and valuation. AMD's quarter was a record: data-centre revenue grew 97% year over year, total revenue was $13.4bn, gross margin 54%, operating income $2.8bn and net income $2.4bn, with Q4 guided at $17bn (+66% year over year) and Lisa Su expecting server revenue to grow faster than 70% in 2027 and data-centre revenue to more than double. He dismisses bear worries about receivables and inventory building as normal for a fast-growing business, noting $4.7bn of free cash flow year to date. The turn comes on valuation: AMD trades at 27x forward earnings, about 39.6x forward price to operating cash flow and about 50x forward free cash flow — roughly three times Nvidia on every multiple — while Nvidia is about ten times AMD's revenue, growing faster (103% versus about 55% year over year) with about twenty times the free cash flow. His DCFs show AMD needs about 51% annual earnings growth at a 25x exit multiple just to return about 10% a year, while Nvidia needs only about 5% growth at 18x. Conclusion: AMD is a great business but priced for tremendous growth, with better alternatives in the industry at current prices; Nvidia offers far more margin of safety. Note: the captioned figures for AMD's earnings path ($12bn in 2026 to $27bn in 2027, $56bn by 2029) and the $1,000 AMD fair value are as captioned and look garbled; 'Lisa Sue' is the captions' rendering of Lisa Su.

calls.video_title: AMD Stock Is Crashing - Is It A Buy Now?
calls.thesis: First tracked Pronk AMD call. Great business with a record Q3 (data-centre revenue +97% YoY, total revenue $13.4B, Q4 guide $17B / +66% YoY, data-centre revenue to more than double in 2027) but priced for tremendous growth: the market prices in ~51% annual earnings growth at a 25x exit multiple just for the stock to deliver ~10% annual returns, and on forward P/E 27x, forward P/OCF ~39.6x and forward P/FCF ~50x AMD is ~3x as expensive as Nvidia on every multiple. There are better stocks in the industry at current prices, and any guidance miss risks underperformance or negative returns.
calls.base: Analysts expect earnings to roughly double in 2027 as data-centre revenue (already ~34% operating margins, an all-time high) keeps outgrowing the rest of the business and expands overall margins.
calls.bull: Bull DCF (88% annual earnings growth to ~$59B by 2029, 25x exit) implies ~$1,000 fair value / ~$1,400 future price, +234% over 3 years — figures as stated in captions; he calls these assumptions extremely bullish.
calls.bear: Even 45% annual earnings growth at a 20x exit multiple produces a negative return from here; the stock is priced for ~51% growth at 25x, so a miss on guidance over the next few years could leave it underperforming or negative.
calls.price_at_call: Down 36% from all-time highs; no share price stated; forward P/E 27x, forward P/OCF 39.6x, forward P/FCF ~50x

calls.video_title: AMD Stock Is Crashing - Is It A Buy Now?
calls.thesis: FLIP: last directional stance AVOID (20 Nov video; most recent entry UNCERTAIN, 24 Nov). Preferred over AMD on risk-reward: ~10x AMD's revenue and still growing faster (103% YoY vs ~55%), much higher margins, ~20x AMD's free cash flow ($149B TTM vs $7B), and ~one-third AMD's price on forward P/E, P/OCF (13.8x vs 39.6x) and P/FCF (15.6x vs ~50x). His DCF shows Nvidia needs only ~5% annual earnings growth at an 18x exit to deliver ~10% annual returns — 'priced as if it is going to stop growing tomorrow', so even modest growth could let it outperform. No explicit 'I'm buying' stated; the stance is a relative preference vs AMD, conditioned on growth continuing.
calls.base: Keeps growing even modestly; priced for no growth, so modest growth delivers ~10% annual returns with a margin of safety.
calls.bull: Analyst DCF (51% annual earnings growth, 25x exit) implies $412 fair value / ~$545 future price; if margins hold and growth continues, today's price proves very cheap.
calls.bear: His earlier AVOID thesis still applies in the background: semiconductors are in his too-hard pile; hyperscaler capex slowdown and custom-chip competition could compress margins.
calls.price_at_call: No share price stated; ~$3.6T market cap; forward P/E ~9 per others he cites, forward P/OCF 13.8x, forward P/FCF 15.6x
